### Item 6 — problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root requests (stated by the customer): R-A move the autopay to Premier 8561; R-B due day 5 -> 20.

Problems and edges:

- **P1 — the 2026-08-05 installment is past due (dpd 9) and must be satisfied by a scheduled payment from an active checking account of the borrower.** Edge P1 -> R-B.
  - Chain: df1a2ef7 "**Loan standing.** The loan must be active and have no installment past due, as the loan record shows" + loan record days_past_due 9 / next due 2026-08-05 + 36f17e38 "The counter goes back to zero when every installment that was past due has been satisfied" + 4befbdc7 (a service that pays "the earliest installment of an auto loan that is past due") -> the due-day change cannot be recorded until the overdue installment is paid. The only visible way the counter returns to zero is a satisfying payment.
  - Mark: **read off** — c3b02a97 states it in one place: "**The due-day move** is available only on a loan that is active with nothing past due, and it places the new day in the month of the loan's next due date. The settling payment is the part that leaves the loan in that condition: it satisfies the installment in arrears, returns days past due to zero and carries the next due date forward on the same loan." Without c3b02a97 the hop would still be derivable from df1a2ef7 + records + 36f17e38.
- **Edge P1 -> R-A (enrollment rate).** 9d04fd66 "The rate written with an enrollment recorded while an installment is past due does not include the autopay discount" + "Days past due are taken from the loan record … as they stand when the enrollment is recorded" + record dpd 9 -> the enrollment must be recorded after the payment for the customer's "whatever discount you are entitled to" to include autopay. Strength: the enrollment is not blocked by arrears (no visible sentence forbids enrolling with dpd>0); what arrears change is the rate written. So the ordering is entailed by "record the rate the loan is entitled to", which requires DPD 0 at enrollment only if the payment is also being made in this conversation — and it is (P1 is forced by R-B). Mark: **read off** — c3b02a97 "**The autopay discount in the new rate** is decided from the days past due the loan shows as that enrollment is recorded, and the settling payment is what brings them to zero."
- **P2 — the old enrollment (drawing on the closed Private Client account) must be ended by the borrower before the new one is recorded.** Edge P2 -> R-A(enroll).
  - Chain: ea9975f6 "Its object is a loan whose autopay is off. A loan never has two enrollments standing side by side, and recording an enrollment neither ends nor takes the place of an enrollment that already stands on the loan" + record autopay_enrolled True on `af221038…` -> enrolling from 8561 needs the standing enrollment ended first; 2393d8ee supplies the cancellation (customer-run). Rate linkage: 0381721c starting rate = "the APR standing on the loan's record at the time of enrollment" + restored discounts, so the enrollment rate is computed from what the cancellation records.
  - Mark: **read off** — c3b02a97 "**The enrollment from the new account** works on a loan whose autopay is off, and it takes as its starting point the APR and discount list that the end of the old enrollment leaves on the loan." (Derivable without it from ea9975f6 + 0381721c.)
- **Edge R-B -> P2 (due-day change before cancellation).**
  - Chain: 2393d8ee "A borrower may be moving autopay to a different checking account and, in the same request, asking for a new due day. In that situation the loan is kept under its standing enrollment for the whole time its payment schedule is being changed; it is never left without autopay while that change is under way" + 2393d8ee "On completion the loan shows autopay as off" -> the cancellation must come after the due-day change is recorded.
  - Mark: **read off** — 2393d8ee states the situation (autopay move + new due day in one request) and the rule in one sentence; c3b02a97 repeats it: "**The end of the old enrollment and the due-day move** are bound by a continuity principle: a borrower moving autopay between accounts is not left without autopay at any point while the loan's payment schedule is being changed."
- **P3 (checked, not a problem) — the 25.00 returned payment fee.** Chain: 9b3bba79 (most recent returned payment fee -> the payment it names: autopay_pcb, posted 2026-08-05, drawn on `af221038…`) + 53186876/a0e51984 test (closing date 2026-08-10 is not earlier than 2026-08-05) -> no bank-error waiver; the fee is simply collected first out of the payment (577f94f9). Mark: **derived**.
- **P4 (checked, not a problem) — late charge.** 5306ff80 + c3097199 NC grace 15 -> none yet, none after paying today. Mark: **derived**.

Resulting tree and order: P1 (pay 2026-08-05 installment, 438.01 from 8561) -> R-B (due day 20, next due 2026-09-20) -> P2 (customer cancels old enrollment at 8.49 / relationship) -> R-A (customer enrolls 8561 at 8.24 / autopay_and_relationship). The order is total and unique.

### Two-way counter-proof

- Support: every value in item 4 is computed from quoted sentences and runtime records; the full sequence succeeds at runtime and leaves the end state c3b02a97 describes.
- Closest alternatives excluded:
  - Due-day change first: excluded by df1a2ef7 "no installment past due" + dpd 9.
  - Enrolling 8561 first / without cancelling: excluded by ea9975f6 "Its object is a loan whose autopay is off".
  - Cancelling before the due-day change: excluded by 2393d8ee continuity sentence.
  - Enrolling before the payment: would record the rate without the autopay discount (9d04fd66 truth table row "above zero | yes | not included"), i.e. 8.49/relationship instead of the entitled rate; excluded given the payment is made in the same call.
  - Paying from the old account: excluded, closed (e528a051 "active status").
  - Waiving the 25.00 returned fee as bank error: excluded by 53186876 boundary "the account was still open on the debit's posting date" (closed 08-10, debit 08-05).
  - Cancellation APR 8.74/none (no relationship retained): excluded by ea3cd1b9 (qualifying account held on funding date, closed afterwards "still counts").
  - Cancellation APR 8.24 carried over: excluded because 6583cd84 says Auto Refinance withdraws the autopay discount on cancellation ("yes"), and b65641af row "yes | yes".
  - Payment amount including the fee on top (463.01): excluded by c3d3d3b0 "The sum still owed is the monthly payment less the standing credit" and 577f94f9 (fees are a share of the payment).
  - Next due 2026-08-20 for the due-day change: excluded because after the payment the current next due date is 2026-09-05 and df1a2ef7 moves it "within the same month as the current next due date".
- "Do only what the customer asked" excluded: doing only R-B is impossible (df1a2ef7 standing test fails on dpd 9); doing only R-A (cancel + enroll) with dpd 9 writes an enrollment rate without the autopay discount (9d04fd66) and leaves the installment past due; doing R-A before R-B violates 2393d8ee continuity. Each exclusion rests on a visible principle + a record — but several of these hops are also stated outright (see item 6 marks), so the exclusion is available by read-off as well as by derivation.

### KB-RUNTIME findings

- **R1 (RED): the visible KB lays out the task's prerequisite chain in one document.** `doc_auto_autopay_source_account_changes_c3b02a97`, section "What each part relies on", gives in a single bullet list: (i) "**The due-day move** is available only on a loan that is active with nothing past due … The settling payment is the part that leaves the loan in that condition"; (ii) "**The end of the old enrollment and the due-day move** are bound by a continuity principle: a borrower moving autopay between accounts is not left without autopay at any point while the loan's payment schedule is being changed"; (iii) "**The enrollment from the new account** works on a loan whose autopay is off, and it takes as its starting point the APR and discount list that the end of the old enrollment leaves on the loan"; (iv) "**The autopay discount in the new rate** is decided from the days past due the loan shows as that enrollment is recorded, and the settling payment is what brings them to zero." Taken together these are all four edges of task 0's tree (both declared `prerequisite` edges and both workflow ordering reasons). A solver can follow this list without working out any hop. Root cause: the SOP document renders the workflow's `dataflow[].carries` and `order_rationale` as one list of dependencies. Evidence: blind items 6 H1/H3/H4 were marked **read off** from this section, and H2 from 2393d8ee/c3b02a97. Affected: c3b02a97, section "What each part relies on" (all four bullets). This red does not change the solution. It removes the task's core difficulty.
- No other KB-RUNTIME condition applies. The visible KB supports "act now" as the source does. It offers no second formula, object or terminal state. It adds no calculation, confirmation, review or step, and drops none. Tool schemas, parameters and owners match the source-layer solution. The declared prerequisites are entailed at hard strength in this world: enroll<-cancel by ea9975f6 "Its object is a loan whose autopay is off"; enroll<-catch-up by 9d04fd66 plus the forced chain payment -> due-day (df1a2ef7) -> cancel (2393d8ee) -> enroll. No document writes task-specific opening world state as policy (all illustrations use hypothetical 2030/2031 dates and invented sums).
- Observation, not a KB defect (reported in policy_kb as source-layer S1): after `post_installment_payment_660c6229` the Premier ledger_balance stays 4382.16. b9b5eac7 says "Payments drawn from a PCB checking account are debited from that account", which faithfully renders base `auto_evt_payment_allocation` "Payments from a PCB checking account debit that account through the payment's trigger" and the base `checking:checking_debit` trigger. The task tool does not execute that trigger. The GT is replayed through the same tool, so no scored value moves.

### Verdict

**KB-RUNTIME RED — R1** (the prerequisite chain is laid out in c3b02a97). The blind solution itself equals the source-layer solution on every value and on the order.
